props.eyebrow: Wedding and event music at Denver Union Station
props.title: The Crawford Hotel
props.lede: The Crawford Hotel is inside Denver Union Station, and its lobby is the station’s Great Hall, with its arched windows and chandeliers. An event here happens in one of the most beautiful spaces in the city.

headingText.html: Trains to the airport leave from just outside, so it’s an easy place for guests who are flying in. This December, our string duo plays the Cooper Lounge for a company holiday party.

props.title: Event spaces at the Crawford Hotel

spaces.name: Cooper Lounge
spaces.facts: The Cooper Lounge is on the mezzanine, one floor above the Great Hall, with about 2,100 sq ft for receptions of up to 80 guests. It has 28-foot cast-iron windows on one side and a view down into the Great Hall on the other.
spaces.why: The Cooper Lounge feels made for a jazz duo.
spaces.alt: The Cooper Lounge on the Great Hall mezzanine, with a curved bar, armchairs and the hall's arched windows behind.

spaces.name: Great Hall
spaces.facts: The Great Hall has high ceilings, arches and chandeliers, with lounge seating and its own bar. It hosts semi-private events of up to 350 guests, or 270 seated.
spaces.why: For a semi-private event in the Great Hall, one guitarist sounds great under those arches and chandeliers.

spaces.name: Webb Gallery
spaces.facts: The Webb Gallery is in the station’s original foundations, about 2,400 sq ft with a built-in bar, for 20 to 150 guests.
spaces.why: Tejas, as a duo for a reception or a full band for a party.
spaces.alt: The Webb Gallery set for a reception, with dressed round tables and cocktail tables under string lights beside a wall of windows.

spaces.name: McWhinney Room
spaces.facts: The McWhinney Room is about 1,050 sq ft, with stone walls from the original foundations, for up to 70 guests.
spaces.why: Spanish guitar for a dinner in the McWhinney Room.
spaces.alt: The McWhinney Room set with round tables and flower centerpieces, with a stone wall along one side.

spaces.name: Terminal Bar on the Plaza
spaces.facts: The Terminal Bar’s plaza is outdoors on Wynkoop Street, facing LoDo, with about 3,500 sq ft and a satellite bar for receptions of up to 220.
spaces.why: Afro house with live tabla, for a party out on the plaza.

props.title: Planning music at the Crawford Hotel

rows.text: Every private event at the station has its own service manager, and an event captain on the day, and we coordinate load-in and setup with them.
The Crawford has AV equipment on site if your event needs more than the band brings.
The hotel’s valet can’t take vehicles over 6'6" or with trailers, so we plan where the act parks and unloads ahead of time.
The Great Hall is the hotel’s lobby and an entrance to the trains, so it stays open to the public. We set the music at a level that works for a shared space.
The station lights its tree at the Grand Illumination each year, and carolers sing in the Great Hall.
There’s valet at the Wynkoop Street entrance, and the A Line to Denver International Airport stops just outside, about 37 minutes away.

props.html: Questions about music at the Crawford Hotel

items.q: How much does live music add to an event at the Crawford Hotel?
items.a: It depends on the act and on how long you’d like music. A solo guitarist for a dinner in the McWhinney Room and a band in the Webb Gallery come out very differently. Our pricing page shows what live music generally costs in Denver, and we can quote your date as soon as you have it.
